subject: Region pinning follow-up — data residency, backups & cross-region failover
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: James Ellison <j.ellison@acmebank.com>, Sana Gupta <sana.gupta@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Region pinning follow-up — data residency, backups & cross-region failover

Hi James / Sana —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet the team and walk through Acme's primary requirements around keeping customer PII and logs in-region, deterministic failover behavior, and backup retention. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the key answers and next steps so your security and infra teams have what they need for the procurement review.

Summary of what we discussed (brief):
- Data residency: Redwood supports region pinning so that inference requests and persistent artifacts (optional KV caches, embeddings, and audit logs) can be stored and processed in a pinned region (e.g., us-east-1 or eu-west-1).
- PII handling: We can support redaction pipelines and customer-side tokenization before hitting our hosted endpoints; if you prefer, the Private deployment gives you full control over PII.
- Logs & audit: Request/response traces and debug logs are stored separately and can be configured to exclude full request bodies; we offer configurable retention (default 90 days, customizable down to 7 days or up to 7 years for Dedicated/Private).
- Backups & cross-region failover: Backups of tenant metadata and optional encrypted snapshots can be stored in a secondary region with an RTO target tied to the SLA. Cross-region failover is supported with configurable warm-standby pools — failover is asynchronous by default and can be configured for stricter consistency with cost trade-offs.

Attachments I've included for your review: redwood_region_pinning_design.pdf (high-level architecture + failover modes) and SOC2_summary.pdf (controls overview).

Open questions we committed to answer:
1) Confirmation of where embeddings-only storage will reside (in-region or secondary region for redundancy).
2) Exact retention windows you need for audit logs vs. debug logs.
3) Whether you require synchronous cross-region replication for KV cache or async is acceptable.

Next steps:
- Marissa (cc'd) will provide technical notes on failover RTO/RPO and recommended configuration for a banking workload.
- Vanessa will scope Dedicated capacity options and pricing for region-pinning with warm-standby.
- James / Sana — can you confirm the security team's preferred retention SLA and whether backups must be single-region or geo-redundant?

I'll follow up with a short mutual action plan once we have those items.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Region pinning follow-up — data residency, backups & cross-region failover

Aditya — thanks for the recap and the docs. Quick answers from our side: 

- Embeddings: must be stored in-region (us-east-1) for at-rest data residency. We can consider geo-redundant backups but primary storage must be resident in the US.
- Retention: audit logs (immutable) should be retained for 7 years for compliance; debug logs can be 90 days.
- KV cache replication: async replication is acceptable for performance reasons, but we need a documented plan for consistency guarantees and an RPO of no more than 1 hour.

Security wants a short write-up on encryption-in-flight and at-rest key management (KMS/HSM integration) and whether keys can be customer-managed. Also need confirmation on whether Redwood's hosted control plane will ever see unredacted PII when region pinning is enabled.

Can you confirm these items and share an updated architecture note that highlights backups + failover timelines?

Thanks,
James
Director, Cloud Engineering — Acme Bank
j.ellison@acmebank.com

Thanks — looping in a couple technical clarifications from the infra team that should help the security ask: 

- Keys: Hosted Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS integration (we currently support AWS KMS and can integrate with BYOK/HSM for Private deployments). When KMS is customer-managed, the control plane does not hold raw key material.
- Control plane visibility: With region pinning enabled, the control plane metadata (routing, model versions, non-sensitive config) is global, but request payloads and tenant-stored artifacts (embeddings, optional KV cache snapshots, and audit logs) can be configured to never leave the pinned region. For hosted customers, we persist encrypted snapshots to regional object stores; metadata references may exist outside the region but do not contain PII.
- Backups & failover modes: We support two backup modes — single-region snapshot (faster restores, lower cost) and geo-redundant encrypted snapshots (secondary-region storage, higher cost). Warm-standby failover uses pre-provisioned capacity in the secondary region; failover RTO can be tuned to target 15–60 minutes depending on pre-warm level.

I'll draft a short security note summarizing the above and a recommended configuration for Acme (embeddings in-region, geo-redundant backups, async KV replication with 1 hour RPO, 15–30 min RTO for warm-standby).

-Marissa
